title: Physics and engineering
competency: Relate physics to civil, mechanical, electrical and chemical engineering and to technology.

keywords.def: Using scientific laws to design and build structures, machines and systems.
The products and processes made by engineering to solve problems.

en.text: Engineering applies physics. Civil engineering uses forces, pressure and gravity; mechanical engineering uses mechanics, thermodynamics and aerodynamics; electrical engineering uses electromagnetism; chemical engineering uses molecular physics and thermodynamics. Technology, in turn, gives physics new tools, like X-rays and rockets, so new physics is found.

screens.title: The Abay bridge
screens.ask: Engineers built the suspension bridge over the Abay. Which physics did they need most?
screens.after:
A bridge must carry its own weight and the traffic safely.
Engineers balance forces, tension in the cables and gravity.
Spectra, echoes and nuclear decay do not hold a bridge up.

screens.title: Physics and engineering
paras: Physics gives knowledge that engineers use: mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics and more.
Engineering branches are governed by physical laws.
Ethiopia built the Axum obelisks and Lalibela churches long ago. Modern physics made skyscrapers and suspension bridges possible.

screens.title: Branches
paras: Engineering branches and the physics they use:

screens.title: Which physics does each engineer use?
items: Forces, fluid pressure and gravity: bridges, roads, dams.
Mechanics, thermodynamics and aerodynamics: engines, cars, aircraft.
Electromagnetism and thermodynamics: motors, circuits, power lines.
Molecular physics and thermodynamics: plastics, paints, fuels.

screens.title: Technology generating new physics
paras: Science and technology are interwoven, like three gears: physics, engineering and technology.
Rockets let us measure in space. X-ray technology helped physics grow.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Using scientific laws to design and build structures, machines and systems.
The products and processes made by engineering to solve problems.

screens.title: Match the engineering branch
screens.why:
Civil engineers build structures that carry loads: roads, bridges, dams.
Mechanical engineers build machines that move: engines, tractors, robots.
Electrical engineers build motors, circuits and power lines.
Chemical engineers turn raw materials into plastics, paints and fuels.
screens.clue: Think of what each engineer designs.
screens.text: Engineering branches: match each branch to what its engineers build.
Physics behind a motor: an electrical engineer designs a motor. The main physics needed is
screens.why:
A motor turns electrical energy into motion.
A current in a magnetic field feels a force.
That force spins the motor's coil.
Electricity + magnetism = electromagnetism.
Answer: electromagnetism.

screens.text: Technology and physics, true or false: technology can lead to new physics.
screens.why:
New instruments make new observations possible.
X-ray machines let us see inside matter.
Rockets carry instruments into space to measure there.
New observations lead to new physics, so it is true.

screens.text: Physics in a solar panel: a solar panel works by
screens.why:
A solar panel is made of photovoltaic cells.
Light falling on the cell frees electrons.
The moving electrons are an electric current.
This is the photovoltaic effect: light → electricity.
Trap: a solar water heater stores heat; a panel does not.

screens.text: Science and technology: Galileo's telescope showed moons going round Jupiter. This is an example of
screens.why:
The telescope is a piece of technology.
It showed moons no one had seen before.
That new observation supported the Sun-centred model.
So the tool came first, and the new physics followed.
Answer: technology leading to new physics.
screens.clue: Which came first: the tool or the discovery?

items.title: Physics in everyday technology
items.why:
A mobile phone sends and receives electromagnetic (radio) waves.
A water pump motor turns by electromagnetism.
A solar panel uses the photovoltaic effect.
A car engine turns heat from burning fuel into work: thermodynamics.
items.text: Activity 1.3: match each everyday technology to the physics it uses.

test.text: Engineering branches: civil engineering mainly uses
test.why:
Civil engineers build bridges, roads and dams.
These must carry loads and hold back water.
So they need forces, fluid pressure and gravity.
Answer: forces and pressure.

test.text: Engineering branches: aerodynamics is used most in
test.why:
Aerodynamics is how air flows round moving bodies.
Mechanical engineers design cars and aircraft that move through air.
So aerodynamics belongs to mechanical engineering.

test.text: Physics and engineering, true or false: engineering branches are governed by physical laws.
test.why:
Every machine and structure must obey the laws of physics.
Engineers use mechanics, thermodynamics and electromagnetism to design.
So the statement is true.

test.text: Technology generating new physics: rocket technology lets scientists
test.why:
Rockets carry instruments above the atmosphere.
There they can measure radiation and fields directly.
So rockets let scientists measure in space.

test.text: Figure 1.12: physics, engineering and technology are shown as
test.why:
Each one drives the others, like gears turning together.
Physics gives laws; engineering uses them; technology gives new tools back.
So the book draws three interlocking gears.

notes.text: p.10 dates the laws of motion to the eighteenth century; Newton published them in 1687.
